Confirmed white eggs, medium size (eggs 50 to 65 g) and German origin in both sources.

history_summary.value: The Deathlayer, or Totleger, comes from the old farm chickens of Westphalia in Germany, mainly around Bielefeld and Herford. It was widespread until more productive foreign breeds arrived and is now seriously endangered, with fewer than 1,000 registered birds in 2016.

summary.value: The Deathlayer, known in Germany as the Westfaelischer Totleger, is an old laying breed from the farms of Westphalia, mainly around Bielefeld and Herford. The grim English name is a mistranslation. It grew out of older words meaning a daily or long lasting layer. Birds come in gold pencilled or silver pencilled plumage and carry a rose comb. They are small and light, with hens around 3.5 to 4.5 pounds and roosters around 4.5 to 5.5 pounds. Hens rarely go broody and lay about 180 medium white eggs a year. The breed is closely related to the East Frisian Gull and the Braekel. Once common, it faded when more productive foreign breeds arrived, and in 2016 fewer than a thousand registered birds remained, so it is counted as seriously endangered. Birds like to roost up in trees when allowed.
